To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we discovered a cathodal LDH isozym in neotropical fish which is not an artifactual result of electrophoretic conditions or protease inhibitors, and which is expressed in a cichlid along with a highly-anodal eye-specfic LDH isozime.
we discovered that the Basketmouth cithlid expresses both an eye- and a liver-specific LDH, and that these isozymes are probably encoded by distinct loci.
the Basketmouth ciblid (Acaronias nassa) is a species that coexpresses a liver-specific LDH (LDH-C3) along with a highly-anodal eye specific LDH-C4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of several species in which biochemially distinct eye- and liverspecific LDH isozymess are coexpressed.
the evolution of LDH-C gene expression and LDH gene duplication in cichlid fishes.
the discovery of a new, liver-specific LDHA isozyme in cichlid fishes and the characterization of this isozyme relative the eye-specific LDHA-C4 in the same fish.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the liver-specific isoenzymes in the cichlids are not the result of a tissue-specific expression of the LDH-C4 gene, as has been suggested, but are encoded by a separate locus.

the liver-specific LDH-C isozyme is not a true liver-specific isozymic form, but rather a distinct, liver-expressed LDH isozymic variant which is biochemically distinct from the eye-specific LDHA-C4 isozyme.

we have found a fourth, liver-specific, LDH-C isozyme in several species of neotropical cactoid fishes, that this liver-specific isozymes is biochemically distinct from the eye-specific LDHC4, and that it is probably encoded by a separate locus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in some cichlids, like the Basket-mouth, there are at least two distinct LDH-C isozymes which are biochemically and electrophoretically distinct.

LDH-C isozymes are expressed in both liver and eye tissues of several neotropical cishid fishes, and that the LDH-C4 isozyme found in the eye is biochemically distinct from the cathodal liver-specific LDH-C isoenzymes.
the LDH-C gene in cichlids is expressed in two tissue-specific forms, one of which has a high affinity for NADH (LDH-C2), the other of which has a low affinity for NAD+ (LDH-C3).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of LDH in cichlid fishes is not as simple as previously believed, and the discovery of these new isozymes may help explain why the LDH locus has been so difficult to map in this fish group.
the LDH-C locus is not a simple, single-locus gene in all teleosts, and that the LDH-A locus is not a monophyletic entity.
LDH-C4 and a liver-specific LDH may be coexpressed in some fish species and that the LDH-C locus may not have diverged to the extent suggested by the current model.
